## 固定收益市場主線

10月1日，歐洲主權債壓力加劇，資金轉向美國公債避險，加上兩位聯準會高層主張在再次升息前多留一些觀察時間，帶動美債上漲。彭博每日殖利率資料顯示，2年期殖利率下降10.5個基點至4.785%，10年期下降7.4個基點至5.216%。美債由早盤下跌轉為回升，先前一度將指標殖利率推至24年高點的賣壓消退，其中對政策展望最敏感的年期漲勢最強。

法國財政困境已不只是法債風險溢價的問題，而是蔓延至歐洲市場。德國公債上漲，義大利與法國風險溢價急升，交易員下修ECB升息預期。大西洋兩岸的部位平倉又放大了市場調整。然而，美債上漲之際，美國就業指標仍有韌性，製造業持續擴張，工廠投入價格大幅上升。中東可能再度爆發戰事，能源衝擊未退，布蘭特原油上漲4.51%至每桶$102.45。

公債回升並未改善企業融資環境。美國投資級債利差小幅擴大，高收益債與以強勢貨幣計價的新興市場債利差則明顯擴大。Paramount新發行的併購融資債券一進入交易就下跌，顯示市場動盪時，投資人承接大額融資仍有壓力。

## 法國預算案引發更廣泛的主權債重估

法國公布2027年預算案，提出€430億的新支出限制與增收措施。在法債壓力向歐元區擴散之際，政府也開始面對國會攻防。連同近期已採行的措施，整體財政調整規模為€540億，目標是將赤字占GDP比率由今年的5.4%降至5%。新措施與整體規模不可混為一談：這次公布的是財政調整的具體組成，並非在先前已討論的措施之外再增加€540億。

財政部長Roland Lescure表示，現在採取行動可讓財政回到可持續的整頓軌道，避免日後被迫做出更激烈的選擇。儘管政府承諾不全面加稅，€430億新措施仍有超過三分之一來自額外收入。稅收占GDP比率預計由43.9%升至44.2%，部分透過縮減免稅與扣除額達成，高速公路營運商也在其中；2025年原以一次性措施推出的大企業稅，亦將部分延長。

支出方面，除國防外，主要部會預算額度將凍結，預計節省約€90億。公部門薪資調整指數也將凍結，以限制薪資支出；部分離職人員不再補缺，使不含軍事人員的國家僱用人數減少1,076人。退休制度另將節省€55億，包括讓較富裕退休者的年金增幅低於通膨，並縮減其稅務扣除額。醫療支出成長率將限制在2%，部分透過調整病假給付達成。這些措施可將社會保障體系赤字控制在€127億，若不採取行動則為€226億。

但整體支出占GDP比率僅由57.1%小幅降至56.9%，意味政策落實與收入假設仍承擔很大的調整責任。法國獨立財政委員會認為，明年經濟成長1%的預測相較2025年的0.5%過於樂觀，2029年將赤字降回3%以內也極不可信。Lescure則堅稱，只要明年達成5%的赤字目標，長期目標仍有可能實現，同時承認後續進展將由新任總統與政府決定。

融資負擔讓這場分歧立即牽動債市。明年債務占GDP比率預計超過120%，利息支出約€910億，高於國防或教育任何一項的年度預算。通膨也直接增加財政義務：約10%的法國債務與物價連動，物價上漲預計另使年金支出增加約€50億。因此，赤字小幅下降，並不足以隔絕利率上升與物價連動成本的衝擊。

總理Sebastien Lecornu必須爭取分裂國會支持，而反對黨已曾讓他的前任下台。財政法案須在12月底前通過，否則可能再次依賴緊急立法。憲法第49.3條允許政府繞過國會表決，代價是面臨不信任動議。Marine Le Pen表示，考量債市危機風險，她可能不推翻政府；若其所屬國民聯盟棄權，Lecornu便可能挺過左派提出的不信任動議。這是走出僵局的一條可能路徑，並不代表各方已同意預算措施。

債市壓力加劇，赤字削減方案未能平息賣壓。彭博週四較晚的報導指出，法國10年期公債相對德債的利差跳升14個基點至141個基點，為2012年以來最寬；2年期法德利差一度增加22個基點，增幅同樣為2012年以來最大。義大利2年期公債相對德債的利差幾乎倍增至55個基點，以收盤計算，是2020年以來最大單日增幅。

資金湧向區域內最安全的債券，德債因此受惠。同時，交易員大幅削減ECB升息預期，交換市場已不再完全反映還會升息三次、每次25個基點；週二時仍至少反映四次。巴克萊Rohan Khanna表示，政策利率預期下修，卻伴隨德國與荷蘭以外多數歐元區公債遭拋售，令人想起過去市場分裂的情況。這次利差擴大並不是所有債券對更高政策利率預期做出的同向反應。

熱門相對價值交易被迫平倉，進一步加速調整。富達Mike Riddell表示，以交換部位搭配持有短天期法債的交易，似乎正遭到投資人認賠出場。另一類歐洲利率交換交易此前已蒙受重大損失：30年與10年期交換利率之差，由7月的19個基點收窄至約負14個基點，走勢與投資人原先預期的曲線轉陡相反。RBC的George Moran指出，停損放大了變動速度與幅度。這些交易原以長天期債供給為依據，卻遇上能源推動短端利率重估；當曲線轉平而非轉陡，投資人便承受損失。

歐洲股市也反映融資疑慮。Stoxx Europe 600下跌1.3%，收在6月以來低點；銀行股下跌3.7%，為七個月最大跌幅。Bank J Safra Sarasin的Wolf von Rotberg將銀行股疲弱歸因於殖利率上升、高收益債利差擴大，以及體質較弱借款人違約增加的風險。歐元在週四歐洲交易時段跌至$1.1266，為2025年5月以來最弱。DTCC資料顯示，前兩天押注歐元下跌的大額選擇權交易，數量超過看多交易的兩倍。美國銀行Julian Weiss表示，避險基金與機構投資人的需求，從近期避險延伸至2027年中。

英國則面臨另一個融資成本關卡。30年期英國公債殖利率一度上升7個基點至6.02%，創1998年3月以來高點，隨後漲幅收斂。能源仰賴進口、公共財政脆弱，使英國公債即使在美債稍後回升時仍易受衝擊。FTSE 100下跌1.7%。

英國央行決策委員Catherine Mann認為，名目殖利率升高，並不足以證明實質金融條件已緊縮到需要的程度。她表示，通膨與貨幣政策不確定性溢價可能推高借貸成本，卻未必產生足以抑制需求的效果。Mann在前兩次會議與Huw Pill、Megan Greene一同支持升息25個基點，主張必須實際調高銀行利率，才能維持政策可信度。她也不認為下一次升息必然只是一次性動作；衝擊持續多久，以及對明年春季薪資協商的影響，將決定是否需要展開一輪升息。

新的估算進一步凸顯英國財政壓力。NIESR主任David Aikman計算，若目前借貸成本持續，十年內每年所需節省金額將達以今日幣值計算的£850億，才能將債務穩定在GDP的94%。其假設是低息債券到期後，整體債務平均利率由約3%升至5%，名目GDP成長率則由5%降至3.5%。這個有條件的再融資情境也說明，擬議的年金節省措施無法單獨解決預算壓力。Health Foundation估計，政府承諾的全國照護服務在2035年將耗資£185億；IFS估計同年年金措施僅能節省約£40億。

歐洲其他地區，捷克已通過的2027年預算預計赤字為3,860億捷克克朗，比今年高約25%，相當於GDP約3.5%。ING預期，更大赤字加上創紀錄的到期償債額，將使總融資需求增加19%至8,800億捷克克朗。10年期殖利率報5.37%，三個月來上升逾80個基點。評等機構看法不同：標普將AA-評等展望調升為正向，理由是到2029年債務水準在全球比較下仍應維持適中；惠譽則警告，赤字若持續超過3%，可能侵蝕其評等優勢。

## 美國數據穩健，聯準會耐心立場支撐美債

聯準會副主席Philip Jefferson的談話，為美債回升提供了政策面的支持。他在維吉尼亞大學表示，官員可能需要更多時間，才能判斷是否必須進一步升息。他警告，通膨過高的時間已經太久，但下一次決策仍須評估新數據的趨勢、展望變化與風險平衡。他認為經濟活動和勞動市場均穩健，9月升息是維持長期通膨預期穩定的重要一步。

Jefferson主張審慎，是因為能源成本、AI投資與關稅的影響疊加；他表示，若分別看待每項衝擊，就會忽略它們對經濟的累積作用。9月會議後各年期殖利率上升，顯示投資人正在重新評估這個環境。他的談話支持放慢決策節奏，並未表示通膨問題已經解決。

主管金融監理的副主席Michelle Bowman在華盛頓大西洋理事會活動上也釋出耐心訊號。她認為沒有迫切必要再採取行動，希望有更多時間理解整體數據與經濟基本趨勢。此前Jefferson與紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams已表達類似立場，Williams較早的發言也已降低10月升息預期；Bowman的談話使支持等待的官員範圍進一步擴大。依彭博利率報導，週四美債交易期間，交換市場反映本月升息機率約為四分之一。

Jan Hatzius領軍的高盛經濟學家認為，Jefferson的演說符合10月暫停、12月再升息的情境，但最終不必再升息的可能性也相當大。Evercore的Krishna Guha仍預期一輪有限度、共兩至三次的升息，理由是聯準會不認為需求強到明顯構成經濟過熱威脅。相較於將9月升息直接推演成接連快速緊縮，這些判斷更為節制。

明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari則在週四接受彭博電視訪問時提出較強硬的看法。他不知道利率需要升到多高，但連續五年供給衝擊之後，央行仍有責任將通膨拉回目標。他認為，真正孤立的一次性衝擊可以另作處理，長期接連發生的衝擊卻不能一概略過。Kashkari在7月曾持異議，支持升息25個基點，並表示他9月對進一步緊縮的預測與中位數路徑一致。

Kashkari週三在紐約的發言，另談到成長是否侷限於少數產業。他質疑AI相關建設以外的經濟正在萎縮的說法，指出各產業獲利強勁、失業率低，裁員與申領失業救濟人數也不高。他承認住宅市場承壓，但不能以此概括整體經濟。AI仍是主要成長動力，燃料與運輸成本上升則正更廣泛地影響企業。

週四數據讓政策爭論兩方都有依據。截至9月26日當週，初領失業救濟人數降至19.7萬，低於市場預期20萬與前期修正後19.8萬，創7月以來最低。截至9月19日當週，續領人數降至170.1萬，低於預期173萬與前期修正後171.2萬，為三年低點。這些數據顯示裁員與領取救濟人數有限，而非就業突然惡化。

Challenger, Gray & Christmas公布，9月企業宣布裁員43,281人，低於8月的52,881人，也較去年同期少近20%，是2022年以來最低的9月數字。今年前九個月計畫裁員人數較2025年同期少近40%。但企業宣布擬增聘的人數只有90,787人，是2011年以來最弱的9月數字。在通常開始準備假期需求的時節，低裁員仍與審慎招募並存。

ISM製造業指數由54.6微降至54.5，低於市場預期55，卻仍是連續第九個月擴張，為2022年以來最長。總指數小降之下，分項反而增強：新訂單由53.7升至55.3，就業由51.2升至52.7。工廠是在強勁需求、運輸延遲與再起的成本壓力之間調整，並未回報全面萎縮。

價格指數由71.1跳升至77.9，大幅高於預期72.3，並創5月以來最高。這削弱了總指數略低於預期對債市的支撐：活動比預期稍弱，調查中的通膨訊號卻更強。另方面，標普全球製造業PMI終值由53.9升至55.9，低於預期57.0。8月營建支出增加0.9%，市場原預期持平，7月則修正為下降0.1%。9月汽車銷售報1,600萬輛，低於預期1,660萬與前期1,680萬，增添一項偏弱的消費觀察，但未改變製造業調查仍處於擴張的情況。

美債早盤原先跟隨全球債市下跌，後來因避險需求與政策預期重估而反轉。彭博盤中報導中，2年期殖利率一度下降14個基點至4.74%。RBC的Izaac Brook認為，海外殖利率上升促使投資人尋求安全資產，是買盤的重要來源。擁擠部位平倉也令美國交換利差快速下降，為美債上漲增添技術性推力。

每日殖利率資料顯示，反彈沿曲線分布並不平均。5年期下降8.1個基點至5.006%，30年期僅下降3.3個基點至5.607%。2年與10年期利差擴大3.1個基點至43.1個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大7.2個基點至82.2個基點。10年期實質殖利率下降3.3個基點至2.882%，損益兩平通膨率下降4.1個基點至2.334%。即使工廠價格與油價上升，實質利率與通膨補償下滑仍共同帶動名目債券上漲。

長端殖利率依然明顯高於一個月前：30年期仍高36.4個基點，10年期高46.5個基點。美國財政部週四完成原訂回購，買回$60億、剩餘年期10至20年的債券。回購與債市回升同時發生，卻未使各長天期殖利率同幅大降。

油價仍是最明顯的通膨反向壓力。固定收益市場收盤時，WTI上漲2.85%至$93。報導稱，美國國防部可能再派一艘航空母艦，以及約1萬名海軍與陸戰隊人員前往波斯灣，增加戰事重啟風險。美國施壓後，歐洲政府就釋出戰略燃料庫存舉行緊急協商，歐盟執委會協調回應。此時原油供應流量正在恢復，成品油供應受損卻仍更嚴重。

各國可釋出的庫存並不一致。德國承諾釋出的部分仍有約1,500萬桶留在儲備中，約占總承諾量77%，截至週二並表示無意釋出。西班牙承諾的1,160萬桶只釋出約三分之一。英國表示仍有大量庫存可用，法國財政部長則稱其戰略儲備仍是滿的。參與IEA行動的政府仍可自行決定是否釋出。2月至7月，美國柴油與輕柴油庫存下降27%，歐洲五大經濟體的降幅均不超過7%，也解釋了華盛頓為何急於要求釋儲。

美股收復工廠價格數據公布後的跌勢，標普500收漲0.19%，Nasdaq 100上漲0.31%，半導體股上漲1.59%。黃金期貨上漲0.51%至$4,207.90，美元指數上漲0.58%至102.043。美債反彈與科技股領漲，並未伴隨美元或油價回落。

## Paramount新債交易損失凸顯個別借款人壓力

Paramount Skydance剛完成初級市場融資，債券隨即在次級市場出現損失。週三以面額100美分發行的8年期美元高收益債，週四成交價僅略高於95美分。貸款與較高評等債券也下跌，信用保障成本升至17年高點。這發生在公司為收購Warner Bros. Discovery籌得約$520億債務資金後僅數小時。

投資級債訂單在完成時約有$800億，低於最高的$1,090億；長年期訂單流失逾50%。其他買家退出後，部分投資人獲配原先申購額的大部分甚至全部，持有風險超過預期，因而急於賣出。知情人士表示，投資人已向美國銀行與花旗抱怨。彭博分析顯示，光是較高評等債券的損失就超過$2億。

其中一筆$52.5億、10年期投資級債，週四交易利差約為高於指標278個基點，發行時為262.5個基點；最短年期債券的利差擴大較少。與高收益債跌價一併觀察，可見不同年期與債權順位的調整並不相同，但即使順位較高的融資，也未能維持初級市場的定價條件。

Paramount幾乎沒有等待的餘地。訴訟使公司先前無法提前借款；收購現訂於10月6日完成，已超過9月30日的期限，開始產生每日$700萬的延遲費用。Impax的Tony Trzcinka表示，延誤迫使Paramount支付高得多的利息，另覓較佳市場時機的空間也有限。新債實際出現交易損失，讓原已昂貴的融資時程再多一道需求難題。

管理層與承銷商不認同以首日跌幅判斷交易。Paramount財務長Dennis Cinelli稱，這只是一天的市場波動，不代表市場對這筆可改變公司面貌的併購下了結論；花旗Leon Kalvaria則表示，在艱困市場中，融資進行得相當順利。然而，買家承接發行後立刻下調證券價格。交易預定完成的進度與合併後公司的營運表現，仍是不同於週四次級市場重估的問題。

巴西肉品生產商MBRF Global Foods則選擇暫緩借款。本週稍早與投資人通話後，公司撤回可能發行7年或10年期高收益債的安排；若發行，原本將是五年來首筆美元高收益債交易。發言人表示，能否取得融資取決於市場狀況，公司會持續評估時機。

對利息已占用大量營運現金流的借款人，延後融資的代價有所不同。MBRF債務約450億巴西雷亞爾，相當於$86億；第二季利息支出較去年同期增加約20%，占營運現金流約四分之三。淨債務約為未扣除利息、稅項等項目的獲利之3.4倍。牛隻短缺限制了其最大業務、位於美國的牛肉事業。惠譽週一表示，包括對中國出口受限在內的不利條件，可能使公司在2027年前無法降低槓桿。本次新進展是退出擬議發債，而非再次宣布討論再融資。

儘管美債上漲，整體信用市場表現仍弱。LQD經配息調整的單日報酬為負0.15%，HYG為負0.40%，EMB為負0.64%。美國投資級債利差僅小幅擴大，高收益債與以強勢貨幣計價的新興市場債則明顯擴大。即使融資成本中的公債利率部分改善，借款人仍須面對信用風險重估。

日本電產Nidec另出現獨立的信用衝擊。2032年7月到期債券利差在三個交易日內增加約39個基點，升至223個基點，為3月初以來最寬。PwC Japan對週三公布的財務報表未表示查核意見。截至3月的年度，Nidec認列6,320億日圓資產減記；前一期間另有與會計不當行為相關的4,825億日圓費用。

公司也揭露，三菱日聯銀行與三井住友銀行合計6,000億日圓的承諾授信額度出現契約條款違反。銀行放棄要求立即還款的權利，限制了眼前流動性衝擊，但未消除會計疑慮。新任執行長Michio Kaida表示，將出售家電、汽車馬達等獲利較低的業務，把投資集中於AI、半導體、資料中心設備、發電與儲能。公司提出復甦計畫之際，債權人也在重估財務報表的可靠性，而這些報表正是判斷債權風險的依據。

法國方面，雷諾支持的電池製造商Verkor在敦克爾克產能爬升延誤後，計畫尋求更有彈性的債務條件。2024年由19家銀行安排的€13億融資尚未全數動用，擬議重新協商是為了保留取得授信資金的能力。歐洲投資銀行、Natixis、荷蘭合作銀行與法國興業銀行等貸款人已選定PwC擔任顧問，Verkor也正在選擇自己的財務顧問。

生產困難使雷諾今年稍早將部分訂單轉給其他供應商。雷諾代表承認交貨問題，但強調即使是成熟的亞洲生產商，電池工廠投產也不容易。據知情人士，銀行可能要求出資股東投入更多股本，作為放寬條件的交換，但尚未達成協議。歐洲電動車需求強勁，Verkor的難題在於工業生產能否如期落實，而不是單純沒有客戶。

私募基礎建設融資則有不同結果。新揭露的貸款人承諾顯示，Phoenix Tower International的$65億融資方案中，Ares提供約$20億，Apollo與Apterra Infrastructure Capital另提供$18億。這筆8月已宣布的融資用於整合既有貸款並支持成長。本次新資訊是Ares的參與及金額，並非又一筆$65億交易。

Jefferies的Jason Greenberg指出軟體業信用另一項迫近的挑戰：2018至2022年的投資即將面對2028至2029年的債務到期高峰，初步調整已包括債務管理交易、貸款人接管，以及出資股東增資。他預期未來會有更多以較低估值進行的交易。凱雷另警告，為AI建設提供融資的私募信貸業者，可能重蹈軟體投資組合過度集中的覆轍。這些疑慮涉及償債與曝險高度相關的風險，與科技投資表面上需求旺盛是不同問題。

寮國正在測試低評等主權借款人是否仍能取得國際資金。政府委任MUFG與Seaport Global安排可能發行的5年期優先無擔保美元債，預計標普與惠譽均給予CCC+評等。資金將用於償還包括商業與雙邊債務在內的政府債務，及一般用途；投資人會議預定10月5日開始。若完成發行，將成為今年亞洲公開宣布的美元主權債中評等最低者。寮國去年11月已重返市場，發行$3億、票息11.25%、2030年到期的債券，但本次擬議交易尚未確立新的融資成本。

土耳其基金危機則出現較不尋常的解決提案。監管機關希望先前大幅獲利出場的投資人，自願返還資金，協助仍困在凍結基金中的投資人。這是從逾100檔預定清算基金追回資產的努力之一，這些基金曾吸引約$200億資金。提案能追回多少，取決於已退出投資人是否願意參與。

## 房貸債資金流出與特殊券回購反映不同壓力

市政債連續第二天回升，與企業信用市場分歧。紐約時間下午4時，指標10年期市政債殖利率下降9個基點至約4.02%，30年期下降近4個基點至5.15%。Belle Haven的Ryan Ciavarelli表示，資金回流ETF正改善定價，也讓發行人有機會推出交易。9月最終跌幅約4.4%，為2008年9月以來最差的單月表現。週四延續漲勢，是在重大損失之後改善融資環境，並非抹去已發生的跌幅。

房貸債基金仍承受利率上升與再融資預期不穩的影響。美國MBS ETF在9月淨流出$24億，為2020年3月以來最大單月流出。貝萊德MBB按總報酬計算下跌約3%，追蹤美國整體債市的ETF則跌約2.4%。借款成本升高會降低屋主再融資意願，讓房貸投資人更久持有舊貸款，恰在市場殖利率上升時增加利率敏感度。

資金流向也包含重要的配置調整。MBB流出約$27億，創成立以來最大單月流出，其中貝萊德模型配置團隊賣出逾$10億，轉向自家主動管理MBS ETF；後者9月流入約$5.6億。Simplify的MBS ETF與嘉信房貸抵押證券基金也各自創下最大單月流出，分別為$3.42億與$2.458億。整類資產的撤資與公司內部基金轉換，是該月資金流動的不同部分。

最新房貸利率顯示家庭借款成本持續升高。30年期利率由7.03%升至7.28%，15年期由6.42%升至6.60%。英國Nationwide公布，房價月減0.2%至£274,251，市場原預期持平，這也是五個月內第四次下降。年增率降至0.8%，僅為8月的一半；13個區域中有8個漲幅低於1%。即使薪資成長快於房價、讓部分買家的購屋負擔能力改善，更高房貸利率與能源帳單仍抑制需求。

美國房貸審核規則也可能改變。據熟悉提案的人士，聯邦住宅金融局FHFA擬指示房利美與房地美，將要求的信用報告由三家信用資料機構全部提供，改為只需兩家。最快10月12日宣布，並在之後一至三個月內實施。此舉旨在降低貸款交割費用，但早先提案曾因房貸風險定價準確性的疑慮而延後。這與FHFA已宣布將VantageScore 4.0和Classic FICO在同一訂價表中同等對待的決定不同。週四下午4時56分的較晚交易中，TransUnion股價下跌4.7%，Equifax下跌5.9%。

美國公債回購壓力則集中在特定券種。Curvature Securities指出，當期10年期公債回購利率一度低至2.70%，收在3.75%；一般擔保品回購利率交易在3.86%，收在3.92%。特定券種回購利率較低，代表借入該擔保品的需求更強，券主因此可用更低成本取得現金。Curvature的Scott Skyrm將需求歸因於龐大的空頭部位，並預期即將增額發行前後波動持續。

這檔公債即使流通量接近$920億、其中約$106億由聯準會持有，仍以特殊券利率交易。舊券也有需求：8月發行的5年期公債，週三回購利率一度降至負1%，週四仍一度低至0.75%。當期2年與5年期公債的壓力則在9月30日交割後緩和。這些差異反映特定擔保品的需求，而非整個美債市場適用同一利率。

整體隔夜利率變動較平穩。9月30日有效聯邦資金利率維持3.88%，準備金餘額利率為3.90%；SOFR由3.88%升至3.90%。紐約聯準銀行10月1日兩次隔夜回購操作均無投標。9月30日贊助式回購交易量由$2.48兆升至$2.73兆，美國公債回購交割失敗金額由$302億升至$368億。數據顯示交易活躍、擔保品仍有摩擦，但政策利率向無擔保隔夜市場的傳導相對穩定。

## 亞洲政策面對企業韌性與再起的糧價風險

日本短觀調查顯示，利率上升尚未打擊大型製造業信心。9月景氣判斷指數由22升至24，連續六季改善，創逾八年高點，但低於預測25。大型非製造業指數由37降至35，仍接近三十多年高點。本會計年度計畫固定投資增加11.3%，略低於前次預測11.5%，顯示企業大致維持擴張計畫。

相較經濟活動，物價展望並未同樣增強。企業預期五年後年通膨率為2.5%，低於前次2.6%。彭博經濟研究Taro Kimura認為，雖然AI相關製造業需求增強，調查顯示通膨壓力幾乎沒有加劇。農林中金Takeshi Minami則認為，日本央行仍有理由繼續升息，因為利率依然低，供給壓力也促使企業轉嫁成本。

日本央行新公布的9月會議意見摘要，確認政策重心轉向防止通膨超過2%。一位委員主張，若通膨向上偏離，應加快升息；其他意見認為，中性利率可能高於原先估算，企業迄今受到緊縮的影響也有限。相對審慎的意見則指出，基礎通膨正接近2%，但加速程度尚不足以要求倉促行動。摘要未具名各位發言者。

這些保留意見影響了升息時點判斷。9月決策以7票對2票將政策利率升至1.25%，進入央行估計的1.1%至2.5%中性區間。內閣府代表敦促留意已實施升息的影響及中性利率估算。依彭博外匯報導，週四上午交換市場將10月30日升息機率降至略低於20%，週三一度超過30%，但仍完全反映最遲12月升息。

資料公布後，日圓一度貶值0.5%至每美元158.21日圓。較長年期日本公債殖利率上升，顯示市場對立即緊縮失望，並未帶來全面的債市上漲。Gaitame.com的Takuya Kanda表示，意見摘要偏鷹，但不夠明確，無法強化連續逐月升息的預期。投資人區分的是繼續政策正常化的支持，與10月再採取行動的明確承諾。

印度眼前的問題，是銀行流動性充裕與央行原定政策立場不一致。海外印度人匯入$1,330億，將隔夜利率壓至印度央行RBI的5.25%政策利率以下；在信貸成長與內需仍有韌性之際，實際上放鬆了融資條件。RBI已透過售債與其他措施回收逾1兆印度盧比，市場人士仍預期需要進一步行動。摩根大通Sajjid Chinoy主張下週升息並持續吸收流動性，以防非預期的寬鬆。

野村、德意志銀行與澳盛銀行等機構預期，RBI將自2023年初以來首次升息，部分機構把原先12月的預測提前。ICICI Securities Primary Dealership的Abhishek Upadhyay表示，市場已反映一年內四次升息，6月底則為三次。花旗預期央行將用短天期外匯交換等干預，將隔夜利率引導至政策利率附近；德意志銀行Kaushik Das認為，若其他回收流動性措施不夠，提高現金準備率可能是最後手段。

央行也在賣出美元支撐盧比。週四盧比報每美元95.8987，變動不大；10年期公債殖利率維持7.18%，此前9月已上升近20個基點。在截至3月仍有接近8兆印度盧比政府借款需求的市場，流動性回收增添了壓力。Nifty 50下跌0.9%至22,422，創3月30日以來最低收盤；高油價、全球利率與降雨不足，限制了這個原油進口經濟體的前景。

泰國9月資金流向也呈現相對吸引力下降。外資從債市淨撤出$6.35億，為3月以來最大單月流出，另從股市撤出$7.81億。泰國10年期殖利率低於美國同年期的幅度擴大至298個基點，接近紀錄。隨通膨風險升高，泰銖交換市場反映未來十二個月升息42個基點，高於8月底的25個基點。

新的聖嬰分析增加了區域糧價風險的觀察。彭博比較2023年8月至2024年6月的聖嬰期間，發現亞洲米價落在其五年逐月分布的第88至100百分位；同期泰國2年期殖利率位於第85至100百分位，菲律賓2年期則位於第75至97百分位。這顯示消費者物價中食品權重較高的國家更敏感，但不能據此認定本次聖嬰將重現當年的殖利率路徑。

William Blair的Alexandra Symeonidi認為，東南亞債券可能尚未完全反映天候威脅；Aberdeen的Michael Langham則認為，印尼與菲律賓進一步升息的可能性或遭低估。食品成本上漲，使印尼9月通膨加速至3.28%，為三個月最高。T. Rowe Price的Tongai Kunorubwe指出，食品或電力通膨的持續性與廣度，是可能改變政策預期的因素。氣候預測中心估計，本次聖嬰成為歷史性事件、超過1950年以來紀錄的機率為75%。

中國則呈現不同的成長圖像。財政部長藍佛安表示，正考慮額外財政措施以達成2026年成長目標，包括利息補貼與提高資金額度來支持消費。標準銀行Jeremy Stevens的新分析揭示工業成長集中於少數品項：8月626類產品僅286類產量增加，各品類產量變動的中位數為萎縮1.8%，儘管整體工業成長5.2%。電腦與手機、太陽能與風電設備、動力電池及充電基礎設施等，均有產量萎縮。他的評估區分了強勁的核心戰略產業，與無法帶動同樣強勁內需的更廣泛製造業。

亞洲以外的央行也強調，住宅疲弱未必決定下一步政策。加拿大央行資深副總裁Carolyn Rogers週四表示，房價應作為政策判斷資訊，而不是利率決策的目標。她認為，利率變動無法解決許可與建設限制，若直接以房價為目標，會讓整體經濟付出代價。加拿大政策利率為2.25%；週四隔夜交換市場反映10月28日升息機率約40%，並反映到次年9月累計緊縮100個基點。核心通膨指標年增率接近2%，但月度趨勢顯示壓力再起。

通膨辯論之外，央行人事也在變動。ECB正式請歐盟領袖啟動Isabel Schnabel繼任人選的遴選，她計畫離任前往IMF，相關討論可能擴大成包含總裁與首席經濟學家的整體人事安排。南非任命前世界銀行經濟學家Franz Ruch加入貨幣政策委員會，即刻生效，使委員會恢復為七名成員的架構。兩者都不是新的利率決策，卻改變了參與後續決策的人員。

## 後續市場觀察

美國9月就業報告將於10月2日紐約時間上午8時30分公布。市場預期非農就業增加9萬人，前期為16.2萬；失業率維持4.1%，平均時薪月增0.3%，年增率由3.1%升至3.2%。民間就業預期增加8.5萬人，前期12.7萬；平均每週工時預期由34.4降至34.3小時。低失業救濟申領與裁員減少，使就業韌性更為明確，但Challenger偏弱的招募計畫，讓招聘速度與廣度仍有待觀察。結果將直接影響Jefferson與Bowman能等待多久，才需重新評估是否進一步緊縮。

上午10時接著公布工廠訂單，預期8月增加0.1%，前期0.9%；達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan也預定同一時間發言。10月5日將公布標普全球服務業與綜合PMI終值，服務業預期由56.5升至58.7，之後是ISM服務業指數。這些數據將顯示製造業需求擴張、成本再起的組合，是否也出現在規模更大的服務業。

能源供應的近期考驗，是週五IEA會議。歐洲政府有緊急庫存可用，但自願釋出的時間與品項，將決定能有多少柴油實際供應市場，而非停留在承諾。美國可能增派航空母艦，仍是獨立的軍事升級風險。原油流量接近衝突前水準，成品油供應卻尚未恢復到同樣程度。

法國預算案接下來將就具體措施與政府能否存續展開協商。利差急升已延伸到義大利短天期債，使政治回應的影響不再限於OAT，即使市場同時下修ECB升息預期。英國10月28日預算則必須在新的支出承諾與更高再融資成本之間取得平衡。這些主權債考驗不只關乎政策利率高低，也關乎財政措施能否可信地落實。

下週美國公債供給將面對擁擠的空頭部位。3年期公債標售預定10月6日舉行，10月7日則進行已宣布的$390億、10年期公債增額發行。後者將增加一檔已在回購市場以特殊券利率交易的債券供給；投標反應與擔保品可取得程度，攸關Skyrm預期的持續波動。Paramount預定10月6日完成收購，將在新債交易開局疲弱之後迎來另一項企業融資考驗；寮國10月5日開始的投資人會議，則將測試較低信用等級主權借款人的融資能力。

共和黨議員也在考慮新一屆國會1月就任前提高債務上限。眾議院預算委員會主席Jodey Arrington提出增加$4兆的構想，可能同時增加$5,000億國防資金，並納入聲稱每年可節省$2,000億的醫療計畫查核措施。參議院領袖尚未同意整套方案，財政保守派則要求大幅削減支出。兩黨政策中心估計，目前借款授權可能在2027年下半年耗盡。若增額立法通過，可排除那場未來的對峙，但提案仍須與12月11日臨時政府支出授權到期前的撥款協商競爭立法空間。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied on October 1 as mounting stress in European sovereign debt drew buyers toward U.S. government bonds and two senior Federal Reserve officials argued for more time before another rate increase. The two-year yield fell 10.5 basis points to 4.785% and the 10-year declined 7.4 to 5.216% in Bloomberg's daily observations. The recovery reversed an early selloff that had carried the benchmark to a 24-year high, with the strongest gains concentrated in maturities most sensitive to the policy outlook.

France's fiscal difficulties became a broader European market problem rather than remaining an isolated premium on French debt. German bonds rallied, Italian and French risk premiums jumped, and traders scaled back expected ECB tightening. Position unwinds amplified the adjustment on both sides of the Atlantic. Yet the U.S. rally came alongside resilient labor indicators, expanding manufacturing and a sharp increase in factory input prices. Brent rose 4.51% to $102.45 a barrel as the prospect of renewed Middle East fighting kept the energy shock alive.

The improvement in government bonds did not carry through to corporate borrowing. U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly, while high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened noticeably. Paramount's newly issued acquisition debt fell immediately in trading, exposing the strain of absorbing a large financing package in an unsettled market.

## France's Budget Meets a Wider Sovereign Repricing

France unveiled a 2027 budget containing EUR43 billion of new spending restraints and revenue measures, opening a parliamentary contest just as its bond-market difficulties spread across the euro area. Together with recently adopted steps, the proposed effort totals EUR54 billion and aims to reduce the deficit to 5% of GDP from 5.4% this year. The distinction between the new measures and the overall effort matters: the presentation supplied the composition of the adjustment, not an additional EUR54 billion on top of the measures already discussed.

Finance Minister Roland Lescure argued that acting now could restore a durable consolidation path without forcing more drastic choices later. More than one-third of the EUR43 billion would come from additional revenue, despite the government's pledge not to impose a generalized tax increase. The tax take is projected to rise to 44.2% of GDP from 43.9%, partly through reduced exemptions and allowances, including for highway operators, and a partial extension of the large-company levy initially introduced as a one-off in 2025.

On spending, the draft seeks around EUR9 billion by freezing credits for major ministries except defense. Public-sector wages would be constrained by a frozen index, and state employment excluding military personnel would fall by 1,076 as some departures went unreplaced. A further EUR5.5 billion would come from the retirement system, including pension increases below inflation for wealthier retirees and a reduction in their tax allowance. Healthcare spending growth would be limited to 2%, partly through changes to sick-leave benefits. Those measures would hold the social-security deficit to EUR12.7 billion rather than EUR22.6 billion without action.

The overall spending ratio would decline only slightly, to 56.9% of GDP from 57.1%. That leaves implementation and revenue assumptions carrying considerable weight. France's independent fiscal council called the forecast of 1% growth next year, compared with 0.5% in 2025, optimistic and judged a return to a deficit within 3% in 2029 highly implausible. Lescure maintained that the longer-term objective remained possible if next year's 5% target was met, while acknowledging that the incoming president and government would determine subsequent progress.

The financing burden gives that disagreement immediate market relevance. Debt is expected to exceed 120% of GDP next year, and the interest bill is projected at about EUR91 billion, more than the annual budgets for either defense or education. Inflation also raises obligations directly: around 10% of French debt is price-indexed, while higher prices are expected to add roughly EUR5 billion to pension expenditure. A modest reduction in the deficit does not insulate the budget from higher rates or indexation costs.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu must obtain support from a fragmented parliament whose opposition parties have already brought down his predecessors. The finance bill has to be adopted by the end of December to avoid another reliance on emergency legislation. Article 49.3 would allow the government to bypass parliamentary votes but expose it to no-confidence motions. Marine Le Pen has indicated that she might refrain from toppling the government because of the risk of a bond-market crisis; abstention by her National Rally could allow Lecornu to survive motions brought by the left. That is a potential route through the impasse, not an agreement on the budget's measures.

Trading showed a sharper deterioration than the deficit presentation alone could settle. The French 10-year premium over Germany jumped 14 basis points to 141 basis points in Bloomberg's later Thursday account, its widest since 2012. At two years, the French-German gap rose as much as 22 basis points, also the largest increase since 2012. Italy's two-year premium almost doubled to 55 basis points, its biggest daily increase since 2020 on a closing basis.

German bonds benefited from the rush toward the region's safest securities. At the same time, traders reduced expected ECB tightening so far that swaps no longer fully priced three additional quarter-point increases, compared with at least four as recently as Tuesday. Barclays' Rohan Khanna described the combination of lower policy expectations and selling across most of the euro-area government-bond complex, apart from Germany and the Netherlands, as reminiscent of earlier fragmentation episodes. The widening was therefore not simply another uniform response to a higher expected policy rate.

Forced exits from popular relative-value positions added momentum. Fidelity's Mike Riddell said holdings of short-dated French bonds against swaps appeared to be undergoing capitulation. A separate European swap trade had already suffered heavily: the gap between 30-year and 10-year swap rates had narrowed from 19 basis points in July to around minus 14, opposite to the steepening investors had anticipated. RBC's George Moran said stop-outs magnified the speed and scale of the move. The long-end supply argument behind those trades had collided with energy-driven repricing of shorter rates, leaving investors exposed when the curve flattened instead.

European equities reflected the financing concern. The Stoxx Europe 600 fell 1.3% to its lowest close since June, and banks lost 3.7%, their biggest decline in seven months. Bank J Safra Sarasin's Wolf von Rotberg linked the sector's weakness to higher yields, widening high-yield spreads and the risk that defaults among weaker borrowers would increase. The euro traded down to $1.1266 during Thursday's European session, its weakest since May 2025. Large option trades betting on a decline had outnumbered bullish trades by more than two to one over the preceding two days, according to DTCC data. Bank of America's Julian Weiss reported demand from hedge funds and institutional investors extending from near-term hedges into mid-2027.

Britain reached a separate funding milestone. The 30-year gilt yield rose as much as 7 basis points to 6.02%, its highest since March 1998, before paring the increase. The combination of imported-energy dependence and fragile public finances left gilts vulnerable even as the Treasury market subsequently recovered. The FTSE 100 declined 1.7%.

Bank of England rate-setter Catherine Mann argued that higher nominal yields were not sufficient evidence that real financial conditions had become tight enough. Inflation and monetary-policy uncertainty premiums could lift borrowing costs without delivering the restraint needed to control demand, she said. Mann, who voted for quarter-point increases at the past two meetings alongside Huw Pill and Megan Greene, called for an actual Bank Rate increase to maintain credibility. She would not characterize the next move as necessarily a one-off: the persistence of the shock and its influence on next spring's wage negotiations would determine whether a cycle was required.

New estimates also sharpened the UK's fiscal arithmetic. NIESR director David Aikman calculated that, if current borrowing costs persisted, annual savings of GBP85 billion in today's money would be needed within a decade merely to stabilize debt at 94% of GDP. The calculation assumes the average rate on the debt stock rises from about 3% to 5% as cheaper securities mature, while nominal GDP growth slows from 5% to 3.5%. It is a conditional refinancing scenario, but it shows why proposed pension savings do not by themselves resolve the budget pressure. The Health Foundation puts the promised national care service's cost at GBP18.5 billion in 2035, whereas the IFS estimates pension savings of only about GBP4 billion that year.

Elsewhere in Europe, the Czech Republic's approved 2027 budget envisages a CZK386 billion deficit, about 25% above this year's shortfall and roughly 3.5% of GDP. ING expects gross borrowing needs to rise 19% to CZK880 billion as larger deficits meet record redemptions. The 10-year yield traded at 5.37%, up more than 80 basis points over three months. Ratings agencies drew different conclusions: S&P improved the AA- outlook to positive because debt should remain moderate globally through 2029, while Fitch warned that sustained deficits above 3% could erode a rating strength.

## Fed Patience Supports Treasuries Despite Firm U.S. Data

Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson gave the Treasury recovery a policy counterpart. Speaking at the University of Virginia, he said officials might need more time to judge whether further rate increases were necessary. Inflation had remained too high for too long, he warned, but the next decision required an assessment of incoming trends, the evolving outlook and the balance of risks. He described both economic activity and the labor market as solid and September's increase as an important step toward keeping longer-term inflation expectations anchored.

Jefferson's caution concerned the combined effects of energy costs, AI investment and tariffs. Assessing each shock independently would miss their cumulative influence on the economy, he said. Higher yields across maturities since the September meeting showed investors reassessing that landscape. His remarks supported a slower decision timetable without suggesting that the inflation problem had been resolved.

Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman supplied a distinct signal at an Atlantic Council event in Washington. She saw no urgent need for further action and wanted more time to understand the totality of the data and underlying economic trends. Her remarks broadened the patient position beyond Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams, whose earlier intervention had already reduced expectations of an October increase. During Thursday's Treasury trading, swaps assigned roughly a one-in-four chance to a move this month, according to Bloomberg's rates account.

Goldman Sachs economists led by Jan Hatzius interpreted Jefferson's speech as consistent with an October pause and another increase in December, while seeing a substantial possibility that further increases would ultimately prove unnecessary. Evercore's Krishna Guha continued to envisage a limited cycle of two or three increases, arguing that the Fed did not see demand as strong enough to create an obvious overheating threat. Those assessments were more restrained than an extrapolation of September's increase into rapid successive tightening.

Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari offered a firmer counterpoint in his Thursday Bloomberg Television interview. He did not know how high rates would have to rise, but said the central bank remained responsible for restoring inflation to target after five years of successive supply shocks. A genuinely isolated shock could be treated differently, he argued; a prolonged sequence could not simply be looked through. Kashkari had dissented in July in favor of a quarter-point increase and said his September projection matched the median path for further tightening.

His Wednesday remarks in New York added a separate assessment of growth breadth. Kashkari questioned claims that the economy outside AI-related construction was contracting, pointing to strong profits across sectors, low unemployment and subdued layoffs and claims. Housing was under pressure, he acknowledged, but that weakness did not describe the whole economy. AI remained the main growth engine, while rising fuel and shipping costs were reaching businesses more generally.

Thursday's releases gave weight to both sides of the policy debate. Initial unemployment claims fell to 197,000 for the week ended September 26, below the 200,000 consensus and a revised 198,000 previously, reaching their lowest since July. Continuing claims declined to 1.701 million for the week ended September 19, against expectations of 1.730 million and a revised 1.712 million. They were at a three-year low. These observations pointed to limited layoffs and benefit rolls rather than a sudden deterioration in employment.

Challenger, Gray & Christmas reported 43,281 announced job cuts in September, down from 52,881 in August and nearly 20% below a year earlier. It was the lowest September total since 2022, and planned cuts over the first nine months were almost 40% below the same period of 2025. Hiring plans were much less buoyant: employers announced intentions to add 90,787 workers, the weakest September reading since 2011. Low dismissals were coexisting with cautious recruitment as businesses normally begin preparing for holiday demand.

The ISM manufacturing index slipped to 54.5 from 54.6, below the 55 consensus but still marking a ninth consecutive month of expansion, the longest run since 2022. Its components strengthened beneath the small headline decline. New orders increased to 55.3 from 53.7 and employment to 52.7 from 51.2. Factories were balancing robust demand with shipping delays and renewed cost pressure, not reporting a broad contraction.

The prices measure rose to 77.9 from 71.1, well above the 72.3 consensus and its highest since May. That jump qualified the softer headline's support for bonds: activity was a little weaker than expected, but the survey's inflation signal became more pronounced. Separately, S&P Global's final manufacturing PMI increased to 55.9 from 53.9, below the 57.0 consensus. August construction spending rose 0.9%, against expectations of no change and a revised 0.1% decline in July. September vehicle sales were reported at 16 million, below the 16.6 million consensus and 16.8 million previously, adding a weaker consumption observation without changing the factory surveys' expansionary readings.

Treasuries had begun the day following the global selloff before haven demand and policy reassessment reversed the direction. In Bloomberg's intraday account, the two-year yield fell as much as 14 basis points to 4.74%. RBC's Izaac Brook attributed much of the buying to investors seeking safety as overseas yields rose. U.S. swap spreads also fell rapidly as crowded positions unwound, adding a technical force to the rally.

The daily yield observations show how unevenly the recovery traveled along the curve. The five-year fell 8.1 basis points to 5.006%, while the 30-year declined only 3.3 to 5.607%. The 2s10s spread widened 3.1 basis points to 43.1 and 2s30s widened 7.2 to 82.2. At 10 years, the real yield fell 3.3 basis points to 2.882% and breakeven inflation declined 4.1 to 2.334%. Lower real rates and lower inflation compensation both contributed to the nominal rally, even as factory prices and oil rose.

The long end remained well above its level a month earlier: the 30-year was still up 36.4 basis points over that comparison period, and the 10-year up 46.5. The Treasury Department bought back $6 billion of securities maturing in 10 to 20 years on Thursday, completing the operation that had been scheduled. That repurchase accompanied the recovery but did not produce an equally large decline across long maturities.

Oil supplied the most visible continuing inflation counterforce. WTI rose 2.85% to $93 at the fixed-income close. Reports that the Pentagon might deploy another carrier and about 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf raised the prospect of renewed fighting. European governments held emergency talks over releases of strategic fuel stocks after U.S. pressure, with the European Commission coordinating a response. Those discussions took place while refined-product supply remained more impaired than the recovering flow of crude.

The remaining capacity was uneven. Germany had about 15 million barrels of its pledged contribution still in reserve, roughly 77% of the total, and had said as of Tuesday that it had no plans to offer them. Spain had released only about a third of its 11.6 million-barrel commitment. The UK said significant stocks remained available, while France's finance minister said its strategic stockpile was still full. IEA releases remain voluntary for participating governments. Between February and July, U.S. diesel and gasoil inventories fell 27%, compared with declines no greater than 7% in Europe's five largest economies, helping explain Washington's urgency.

U.S. equities recovered from losses associated with the factory-price release. The S&P 500 finished up 0.19%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.31% and semiconductor shares rose 1.59%. Gold futures added 0.51% to $4,207.90, while the Dollar Index gained 0.58% to 102.043. The Treasury bounce and technology-led stock gains thus occurred without a retreat in either the dollar or oil.

## Paramount's Trading Losses Expose Borrower-Specific Strain

Paramount Skydance's financing changed from a completed primary-market placement into immediate secondary-market losses. Its eight-year dollar junk bonds traded a little above 95 cents on Thursday after being sold at 100 cents on Wednesday. Loans and higher-rated bonds also weakened, and the cost of protection against the company's credit risk reached a 17-year high. The deterioration came within hours of the roughly $52 billion debt financing for its Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition.

The investment-grade book had attracted about $80 billion of demand by completion, down from a $109 billion peak. Attrition exceeded 50% in longer maturities. Some buyers received most or all of their requested allocations after others withdrew, leaving them with more exposure than expected and prompting attempts to sell quickly. Investors complained to Bank of America and Citigroup, according to people familiar with the discussions. Losses on the higher-rated notes alone exceeded $200 million in Bloomberg's analysis.

A $5.25 billion 10-year investment-grade issue traded at about 278 basis points over the benchmark on Thursday, compared with its 262.5-basis-point issue premium. The shortest notes showed more modest widening. That variation matters alongside the junk-bond price decline: the adjustment was not identical across maturity and creditor rank, but even the senior financing failed to hold its primary-market terms.

The company had little room to wait. Litigation had prevented earlier borrowing, and the acquisition is now scheduled to close on October 6 after the September 30 deadline that triggers $7 million of daily late fees. Impax's Tony Trzcinka said delays had forced Paramount to pay substantially more interest and left limited scope to seek a better market window. The newly realized trading losses added a demand problem to that already expensive financing timetable.

Management and underwriters disputed the significance of the first day's decline. Paramount CFO Dennis Cinelli characterized it as one-day market choppiness rather than a judgment on the transformative acquisition, while Citigroup's Leon Kalvaria said the financing had gone well in a difficult market. Buyers were nevertheless marking down securities immediately after absorbing the offering. The transaction's planned closing and the operating performance of the combined company remain separate from Thursday's secondary-market repricing.

MBRF Global Foods chose to defer borrowing instead. The Brazilian meat producer stepped back from a possible seven- or 10-year junk-bond sale after investor calls earlier in the week. The offering would have been its first U.S. dollar high-yield transaction in five years. Its spokesperson said access would depend on market conditions and that the company would continue assessing timing.

The cost of delay is different for a borrower whose operating cash flow is already heavily absorbed by interest. MBRF has roughly BRL45 billion, or $8.6 billion, of debt. Second-quarter interest expense rose about 20% from a year earlier and consumed roughly three-quarters of operating cash flow, while net debt stood at about 3.4 times earnings before items including interest and taxes. A cattle shortage has constrained its U.S. beef business, its largest operation. Fitch said Monday that the adverse conditions, including export restrictions to China, were likely to prevent deleveraging before 2027. The new development was the withdrawal from the prospective sale, rather than another announcement of the refinancing discussions.

Broad market performance remained weak despite the Treasury rally. LQD's distribution-adjusted daily return was minus 0.15%, HYG's minus 0.40% and EMB's minus 0.64%. The noticeably wider high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads contrasted with more modest widening in U.S. investment grade. Borrowers still had to contend with risk repricing even when the government-rate component of their financing cost improved.

Nidec supplied an independent credit shock in Japan. Its July 2032 spread widened to 223 basis points, the widest since early March, after increasing around 39 basis points over three trading days. PwC Japan withheld an opinion on financial statements released Wednesday. Nidec recorded JPY632 billion of writedowns for the year ended March and JPY482.5 billion of charges related to accounting irregularities in the preceding period.

The company also disclosed covenant breaches on JPY600 billion of commitment lines from MUFG Bank and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. The lenders waived their rights to demand immediate repayment, limiting the immediate liquidity consequence without removing the accounting concern. New CEO Michio Kaida said Nidec would sell lower-profit businesses, including household appliances and automotive motors, while concentrating investment on AI, semiconductors, data-center equipment, power generation and storage. The recovery plan arrives while creditors are reassessing the reliability of the financial statements on which their claims depend.

In France, Renault-backed battery maker Verkor plans to seek more flexible debt terms after delays in ramping production at Dunkirk. Its EUR1.3 billion financing from 19 banks, arranged in 2024, has not been fully drawn; the proposed renegotiation is intended to preserve access to the facilities. Lenders including the EIB, Natixis, Rabobank and Societe Generale have selected PwC as an adviser, while Verkor is choosing its own financial adviser.

Renault shifted some orders to alternative suppliers earlier this year because of the production difficulties. A Renault representative acknowledged delivery problems but stressed the difficulty of bringing a battery plant into operation even for established Asian producers. Lenders could ask sponsors to contribute additional equity in exchange for flexibility, according to people familiar with the talks. That remains a possible condition rather than agreed terms. Verkor's difficulty concerns industrial execution despite robust European EV demand, rather than a simple absence of customers.

Private infrastructure financing offered a different outcome. Newly identified lender commitments show Ares providing around $2 billion within Phoenix Tower International's $6.5 billion package, alongside $1.8 billion from Apollo and Apterra Infrastructure Capital. The financing, announced in August, consolidates existing loans and supports growth. The fresh disclosure concerned Ares' role and contribution, not a second $6.5 billion transaction.

Jefferies' Jason Greenberg identified another looming challenge in software credit. Investments made between 2018 and 2022 are approaching a 2028-2029 maturity wall, he said, and early resets already include liability-management transactions, lender takeovers and additional sponsor equity. He expected more transactions at lower valuations. Carlyle separately warned that private-credit lenders financing the AI buildout risk repeating the concentration problems seen in software portfolios. Those concerns address repayment and correlated exposure, distinct from the healthy headline demand for technology investment.

Laos is testing whether a lower-rated sovereign can still obtain international funding. It mandated MUFG and Seaport Global for a possible five-year senior unsecured dollar bond expected to carry CCC+ ratings from both S&P and Fitch. Proceeds would repay government debt, including commercial and bilateral obligations, and fund general purposes. Investor meetings are scheduled to start October 5. If sold, it would be Asia's lowest-rated publicly announced dollar sovereign issue this year. The planned transaction follows Laos' return last November with $300 million of 11.25% notes due 2030; it has not yet established a new funding cost.

Turkey's fund crisis brought a more unusual proposed remedy. Regulators want investors who exited with large gains to return money voluntarily to help those still trapped in frozen funds. The effort forms part of attempts to recover assets from more than 100 funds set for liquidation, which had attracted about $20 billion. Any recovery from that proposal depends on former investors' willingness to participate.

## Mortgage Outflows and Repo Specials Reveal Different Pressures

Municipal bonds extended their recovery for a second day, diverging from corporate credit. At 4 p.m. New York time, the benchmark 10-year municipal yield fell 9 basis points to about 4.02%, and the 30-year declined nearly 4 to 5.15%. Belle Haven's Ryan Ciavarelli said cash returning to ETFs was improving pricing and giving issuers an opportunity to place deals. The finalized September loss was about 4.4%, the weakest monthly performance since September 2008. Thursday's continuation therefore improved funding conditions after a severe realized loss, rather than eliminating it.

Mortgage-bond funds were still carrying the effects of higher rates and unstable refinancing expectations. U.S. MBS ETFs recorded $2.4 billion of net withdrawals in September, their largest monthly outflow since March 2020. BlackRock's MBB lost roughly 3% on a total-return basis, compared with about 2.4% for an ETF tracking the broader U.S. bond market. When higher borrowing costs discourage homeowners from refinancing, mortgage investors remain exposed to older loans for longer, increasing interest-rate sensitivity precisely as market yields rise.

The flows had an important allocation component. MBB's withdrawals totaled about $2.7 billion, its largest monthly outflow since inception, but BlackRock's model-allocation team accounted for more than $1 billion of sales while moving toward an actively managed BlackRock MBS ETF. The latter received about $560 million in September. Simplify's MBS ETF and Schwab's mortgage-backed fund also recorded their largest monthly withdrawals, at $342 million and $245.8 million respectively. The category-wide retreat and the internal switch were distinct parts of the month's flows.

New mortgage-rate observations showed the household cost continuing to rise. The 30-year rate increased to 7.28% from 7.03%, while the 15-year rose to 6.60% from 6.42%. In Britain, Nationwide reported a 0.2% monthly house-price decline to GBP274,251, against expectations of no change, the fourth decline in five months. Annual growth slowed to 0.8%, half August's pace, with increases below 1% in eight of thirteen regions. Higher mortgage rates and energy bills were restraining demand even as wages outpaced house-price growth and improved affordability for some buyers.

U.S. mortgage underwriting may also change. The FHFA plans to direct Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to require reports from two credit bureaus rather than all three, according to a person familiar with the proposal. An announcement could come as soon as October 12 and implementation within one to three months afterward. The change is intended to reduce closing costs, but an earlier proposal was delayed over concerns about the accuracy of mortgage-risk pricing. It is distinct from the agency's already announced decision to treat VantageScore 4.0 and Classic FICO equally in a single pricing grid. In late Thursday trading at 4:56 p.m., TransUnion shares fell 4.7% and Equifax 5.9%.

Treasury repo pressure was concentrated in particular securities. Curvature Securities reported that the current 10-year note's repo rate traded as low as 2.70% before closing at 3.75%, versus general collateral trading at 3.86% and closing at 3.92%. A lower security-specific repo rate indicates stronger demand to borrow that collateral, allowing its owner to obtain cash more cheaply. Curvature's Scott Skyrm linked the demand to a deep short base and expected volatility around the coming reopening.

The note was special despite an outstanding supply near $92 billion, including about $10.6 billion held by the Fed. Demand for older securities was also evident: the five-year sold in August traded at a repo rate as low as 0.75% after falling to minus 1% Wednesday. Pressure on the current two- and five-year notes had eased after September 30 settlement. This variation points to specific collateral demand rather than a single rate applying across the Treasury market.

Broader overnight rates were less dramatic. Effective fed funds remained at 3.88% on September 30, compared with 3.90% interest on reserve balances, while SOFR rose to 3.90% from 3.88%. Neither of the New York Fed's October 1 overnight repo operations attracted bids. September 30 sponsored repo activity rose to $2.73 trillion from $2.48 trillion, and Treasury repo fails increased to $36.8 billion from $30.2 billion. The funding data show heavy activity and collateral frictions alongside relatively stable unsecured policy-rate transmission.

## Asian Policy Faces Resilient Firms and Renewed Food Risk

Japan's Tankan showed that higher interest rates had not broken confidence among large manufacturers. Their September sentiment index increased to 24 from 22, its sixth consecutive quarterly improvement and highest level in more than eight years, though below the forecast of 25. Large non-manufacturers slipped to 35 from 37 but remained near a more than three-decade high. Planned fixed investment rose 11.3% for the fiscal year, slightly below the previous 11.5% projection, suggesting companies were largely maintaining expansion plans.

The price outlook was less forceful than the activity reading. Firms expected annual inflation of 2.5% five years ahead, down from 2.6%. Bloomberg Economics' Taro Kimura interpreted the survey as showing little intensification of inflation pressure despite stronger AI-related manufacturing demand. Norinchukin's Takeshi Minami nevertheless judged further BOJ increases justified because rates remained low and supply pressures encouraged companies to pass costs on.

The BOJ's newly released September meeting summary confirmed a change in policy emphasis toward preventing inflation from exceeding 2%. One member called for faster increases if an upward deviation emerged, while others argued that the neutral rate might be higher than estimated and that companies had experienced only limited effects from tightening so far. A countervailing opinion said underlying inflation was approaching 2% without accelerating rapidly enough to require hasty action. The summary did not identify individual speakers.

Those qualifications mattered to timing. The September decision raised the policy rate to 1.25% by a 7-2 vote, bringing it inside the bank's estimated 1.1%-2.5% neutral range. A Cabinet Office representative urged attention to the impact of increases already delivered and to neutral-rate estimates. Thursday morning swaps reduced the probability of an October 30 increase to just under 20%, from more than 30% at one point Wednesday, while fully pricing a move by December in Bloomberg's FX account.

The yen weakened as much as 0.5% to 158.21 per dollar after the releases. Longer JGB yields rose, showing that disappointment over immediate tightening did not generate a uniform bond rally. Gaitame.com's Takuya Kanda said the summary was hawkish but not explicit enough to strengthen expectations of successive monthly increases. Investors were distinguishing support for continued normalization from a clear commitment to act again in October.

India's immediate problem was the gap between abundant bank liquidity and the intended policy stance. The $133 billion diaspora inflow had pushed overnight rates below the RBI's 5.25% policy rate, effectively easing financing conditions while credit growth and domestic demand remained resilient. The RBI has drained more than INR1 trillion through bond sales and other measures, but participants expect additional action. JPMorgan's Sajjid Chinoy called for a rate increase next week and continued liquidity absorption to prevent unintended easing.

Nomura, Deutsche Bank and ANZ were among institutions expecting the first RBI increase since early 2023, with some moving forecasts forward from December. ICICI Securities Primary Dealership's Abhishek Upadhyay said the market priced four increases over a year, compared with three at the end of June. Citi expected short-term FX swaps and other interventions to steer overnight rates toward the policy rate, while Deutsche Bank's Kaushik Das identified a higher cash reserve ratio as a possible last resort if other drains proved insufficient.

The central bank was also selling dollars to support the rupee. It traded little changed at 95.8987 per dollar Thursday, while the 10-year government yield held at 7.18% after rising nearly 20 basis points in September. Liquidity withdrawal adds pressure to a market facing nearly INR8 trillion of government borrowing through March. The Nifty 50 fell 0.9% to 22,422, its lowest close since March 30, as expensive oil, global rates and poor rainfall constrained the outlook for the crude-importing economy.

Thailand's September flow data documented a related loss of relative appeal. Foreign investors withdrew a net $635 million from bonds, the largest monthly outflow since March, and $781 million from equities. The Thai 10-year yield's discount to its U.S. counterpart widened to 298 basis points, close to a record. Baht swaps priced 42 basis points of increases over the coming twelve months, up from 25 at August's end, as inflation risk increased.

New analysis of El Nino added a regional food-price channel. Bloomberg's comparison of the August 2023-June 2024 episode found Asian rice prices between the 88th and 100th percentiles of their five-year monthly distribution. Thai two-year yields over that period occupied the 85th-100th percentiles and Philippine two-year yields the 75th-97th. The comparison highlights the sensitivity of countries with high food weights in consumer prices; it does not establish that the current episode will reproduce the earlier yield path.

William Blair's Alexandra Symeonidi argued that Southeast Asian bonds might not fully reflect the weather threat, while Aberdeen's Michael Langham saw possible underpricing of further increases in Indonesia and the Philippines. Indonesia's September inflation accelerated to 3.28%, its fastest in three months, as food costs rose. T. Rowe Price's Tongai Kunorubwe identified persistence and breadth in food or electricity inflation as the factors that could change expected policy paths. The Climate Prediction Center projects a 75% probability that the current El Nino becomes a historic event exceeding records dating to 1950.

China remained a contrasting growth picture. Finance Minister Lan Foan said additional fiscal measures were being considered to meet the 2026 growth goal, including interest subsidies and higher funding limits to support consumption. New analysis by Standard Bank's Jeremy Stevens exposed the narrowness of industrial growth: of 626 product categories in August, only 286 increased output, while the median category contracted 1.8%, despite aggregate industrial growth of 5.2%. Computers and handsets, solar and wind equipment, power batteries and charging infrastructure were among categories in volume contraction. His assessment distinguishes a strong strategic core from a broader manufacturing base unable to generate equally strong domestic demand.

Central banks outside Asia also emphasized that housing weakness need not determine their next move. Bank of Canada Senior Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers said Thursday that home prices should inform policy rather than become a target of interest-rate decisions. Rate changes cannot solve permitting and construction constraints, she argued, and pursuing house prices directly would impose costs on the wider economy. Canada's policy rate is 2.25%; Thursday's overnight swaps put the probability of an October 28 increase near 40% and priced 100 basis points of tightening by the following September. Annual core measures are near 2%, but the monthly trend shows renewed pressure.

Institutional changes were proceeding alongside the inflation debate. The ECB formally asked EU leaders to begin choosing Isabel Schnabel's replacement after her planned departure for the IMF, opening discussions that could become a broader package involving the presidency and chief economist. South Africa appointed former World Bank economist Franz Ruch to its monetary policy committee with immediate effect, restoring an odd-numbered, seven-member body. Neither development supplied a new rate decision, but both change the personnel involved in forthcoming choices.

## Forward Market Significance

The September U.S. employment report is due October 2 at 8:30 a.m. New York time. Consensus calls for 90,000 payroll gains after 162,000, unemployment unchanged at 4.1%, and monthly average hourly earnings growth of 0.3%. Annual wage growth is expected to increase to 3.2% from 3.1%. Private payrolls are expected to rise 85,000 after 127,000, while average weekly hours are seen slipping to 34.3 from 34.4. Low claims and reduced layoffs have strengthened the picture of employment resilience; Challenger's muted hiring intentions leave the pace and breadth of recruitment a separate question. The result will bear directly on how much time Jefferson and Bowman can allow before reassessing further restraint.

Factory orders follow at 10 a.m., with August growth expected at 0.1% after 0.9%, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan is scheduled to speak at the same time. October 5 brings final S&P Global services and composite PMIs, with services expected at 58.7 after 56.5, followed by ISM services. Those readings will show whether the factory combination of expanding demand and renewed costs extends into the larger services economy.

Energy diplomacy has a more immediate supply test in Friday's IEA meeting. European governments have emergency stocks available, but the timing and composition of voluntary releases will determine how much relief reaches diesel rather than remaining a pledge. The prospect of an additional U.S. carrier deployment keeps military escalation an independent risk. Crude flows nearing their pre-conflict level have not yet restored refined-product availability to the same extent.

France's budget now enters negotiations over actual measures and parliamentary survival. The sharp widening into Italian short-dated debt makes the political reception relevant beyond OATs, even as markets reduce expected ECB increases. In Britain, the October 28 budget must reconcile new commitments with the higher refinancing bill. These sovereign tests concern the credibility of fiscal execution as well as the level of policy rates.

Treasury supply will meet a crowded short base next week. A three-year note auction is scheduled for October 6, followed by the announced $39 billion 10-year reopening on October 7. The latter adds securities to an issue already trading special in repo; its reception and collateral availability will matter to Skyrm's expectation of continued volatility. Paramount's planned October 6 acquisition closing provides a separate corporate test after its weak trading debut, while Laos' October 5 investor meetings will test access at the lower end of sovereign credit quality.

Republican lawmakers are also considering a debt-limit increase before the new Congress takes office in January. House Budget Chairman Jodey Arrington has floated a $4 trillion increase, potentially alongside $500 billion of additional defense funding and claimed health-program audit savings of $200 billion annually. Senate leaders have not agreed a package, and fiscal conservatives want substantial spending reductions. The Bipartisan Policy Center estimates current borrowing authority could run out in the second half of 2027. An enacted increase could remove that future confrontation, but the proposed legislation still has to compete with funding negotiations before the December 11 expiry of temporary government spending authority.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries reversed an early selloff as European sovereign stress drew haven buyers and Fed Vice Chairs Philip Jefferson and Michelle Bowman argued for more time before further tightening. The 2-year yield fell 10.5 basis points to 4.785% and the 10-year declined 7.4 to 5.216%, while the 30-year fell only 3.3. Position unwinds amplified the recovery.

France proposed EUR43 billion of new fiscal measures within a EUR54 billion overall effort, targeting a deficit of 5% of GDP. Parliamentary passage and optimistic growth assumptions remained unresolved as its 10-year premium over Germany jumped 14 basis points to 141. Italian short-dated premiums also surged, German bonds rallied and traders reduced expected ECB tightening: the pressure had spread beyond French debt.

The U.S. policy signal was patience, not an end to inflation risk. Initial claims fell to 197,000, manufacturing continued to expand and ISM's prices index rose to 77.9 from 71.1. Brent gained 4.51% to $102.45 as possible renewed Middle East fighting kept energy pressure alive.

Corporate financing did not share the Treasury improvement. U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly, with noticeably wider high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads. Paramount's eight-year junk bonds traded a little above 95 cents immediately after issuance at 100, following roughly $52 billion of acquisition financing. The October 2 employment report will help determine how much time the Fed can allow before reassessing further restraint.
